title: Telangana Police “Darpan” face-matching reunites Som Soni with his family after five years
summary: Darpan matched Som Soni, missing from Allahabad since 14 July 2015, to a boy in a Goalpara, Assam child home; reunited October 2020.
account: Darpan, a facial-recognition tool built by Telangana State Police, matches photographs of missing children against photographs of children lodged in child homes across the country. A routine matching run matched Som Soni to a boy police had found on 23 July 2015. He had been admitted to a child welfare center at Goalpara, Assam (spelled “Golapara” in the reports). Soni had gone missing from his home in Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh) on 14 July 2015 aged eight. ETV Bharat describes him as a resident of Handia in Allahabad. The case lay with Handia police station. Telangana Police notified Handia police. His parents traveled to Goalpara and identified him. The case was announced on 9 October 2020 by Swati Lakra, ADGP of the Telangana Police Women Safety Wing. The exact day of the reunion is not given.
purpose: Darpan was built to match missing-child photographs with children found in institutions so they can be returned to their families. This reunification is that intended benefit.
system: Darpan face-recognition portal for missing and found children
deployer: Telangana State Police, with Goalpara Police (Assam) and Handia Police Station (Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh)
domain: Policing / missing persons and child protection
taxonomy_note: The good is a family reunited, and the type names the identity match that located the boy.

ratings.reason: A child separated from his parents for five years, living in an institution in another state, was identified and returned to his family. The sources describe the match as having “changed the lives of the child and his parents”.

ai_role.statement: The face match was the sole lead. The boy had been in an Assam institution for five years with no identification until Darpan matched his photograph to the Uttar Pradesh missing-child record. Police then contacted the parents. Verification rested on the parents identifying him in person. The Telangana CID news page was not available. So the record relies on news reports quoting the ADGP.

fields.account: Darpan, a facial-recognition tool built by Telangana State Police, matches photographs of missing children against photographs of children lodged in child homes across the country. A routine matching run matched Som Soni to a boy police had found on 23 July 2015. He had been admitted to a child welfare center at Goalpara, Assam (spelled “Golapara” in the reports). Soni had gone missing from his home in Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh) on 14 July 2015 aged eight. ETV Bharat describes him as a resident of Handia in Allahabad. The case lay with Handia police station. Telangana Police notified Handia police. His parents traveled to Goalpara and identified him. The case was announced on 9 October 2020 by Swati Lakra, ADGP of the Telangana Police Women Safety Wing. The exact day of the reunion is not given.
